newsitem.title: USA: Kemp says debate will be Dole unfiltered.
newsitem.headline: Kemp says debate will be Dole unfiltered.

text.p: The televised presidential debate will give audiences a chance to see Bob Dole "unfiltered," running mate Jack Kemp and his campaign director said on Sunday.
"Bob Dole gets the first chance to speak without a filter," Kemp said on NBC Television's "Meet the Press" programme, "to share the vision that he has."
Dole campaign director Donald Rumsfeld, appearing on "Fox News Sunday," did not rule out a "mystery guest" in the audience at the site of the Hartford debate aimed at rattling President Clinton.
Asked about reports the Dole campaign planned to put someone in the audience to shake Clinton, Rumsfeld said: "We'll have to see" with a broad grin on his face.
He echoed Kemp's unfiltered line, saying: "It will be Bob Dole unfiltered by the media, unfiltered by negative ads."

Asked if Dole's reputation for biting sarcasm might be a hindrance in his one-on-one with Clinton, Kemp said that "Bob Dole is not a mean man" and offered a more hopeful programme for the country than the president.
"It is his opportunity to share that vision without the interlocutors of the press," Kemp said.
Using football analogies, the former Buffalo Bills and San Diego Chargers quarterback said Dole was trailing, but could overtake Clinton in the remaining weeks of the campaign.
"It is the middle of the third quarter and we are a touchdown behind," Kemp said. "Clinton is sitting on the ball," he added, promoting the status quo.
